column10: You really need to know what acids are in your products before use. I see a lot of comments about how this product dries your skin out. First, a TINY dab on the finger of acid based cleansers is good enough to cut deep in acne prone skin. You don?ôt need a full pump size to cleanse! The trick is use small circular motions over troubled areas and then rise with COLD water. Second, this product contains BOTH glycolic acid salicylic acid.Glycolic acid has the smallest molecule in the AHA family, meaning it can penetrate deep into even those tiny hard to reach pores. This acid is great at helping with fine lines, uneven textures, and elasticity of the skin. This acid also helps pull moisture to the surface of skin. However, it can be irritating for sensitive skin types.Salicylic acid goes is great for oil, it evens pore texture and size. It?ôs amazing for bad acne and black head build ups. It also has skin soothing attributes. Take both of these acids and you will find that this product is designed just as advertised, to tighten and tone uneven textures plus pores. Again, remember that this is a powerhouse. A little goes a long way and too much will strip your skin of it?ôs natural balance. If this combination is drying your skin out despite using small amounts and using it every other day versus everyday, consider the Irish Moor Mud Purifying Cleanser Gel from Peter Thomas Roth. That serum is produced with both lactic and glycolic acid. Lactic acid also pulls moisture to the skin but is on the gentler end. I switch off between these two serums. Always make sure you are wearing sunscreen while using any products with acids. A natural toner such as witch hazel can be useful at boosting a safe PH level after after cleansing.

column10: You really need to know what acids are in your products before use. I see a lot of comments about how this product dries your skin out. First, a TINY dab on the finger of acid based cleansers is good enough to cut deep in acne prone skin. This acid is great at helping with fine lines, uneven textures, and elasticity of the skin. This acid also helps pull moisture to the surface of skin. column10: This might be a hot take, but I actually really like that C-Firma is now packaged so that the user can mix the product when it arrives. While the mixing process can be tedious and user-error prone, it allows the consumer to use the product at its maximum potency, meaning that we?ôre getting the most for our money. In the past, the C-Firma I would receive would already be a slight orange colour (meaning it had already started oxidizing and is losing potency). Now, immediately after mixing, it is clear (which is how it should be). I personally had a really positive experience mixing the serum, so thought I could share my process:1)	Plan to mix the serum at least a day before you intend to use it. I mixed it 3 days in advance.2)	Tap the container with the powder on a hard flat surface so that the powder settles at the bottom of the container. This helps to prevent powder from making its way onto the threaded part where the container joins with the dispensing head when opening to add the liquid.3)	When you open the container with the powder, do so very carefully4)	Slowly pour the liquid into the container with the powder5)	Close the container tightly before shaking ??you want to make sure that it is totally and fully sealed, or you?ôll end up with a leaky mess! 6)	Shake heaps. Heaps and heaps. If there is powder still at the bottom, don?ôt fret. You can either continue to shake, or you can leave it be for some time. That powder should dissolve on its own over time. The shaking is really only speeding up the dissolution process.7)	Occasionally shake until powder is fully dissolved8)	Let the contents settle in the fridge. Once ?úfoam??disappears, just give it a good shake before using. Another note: this serum smells like hotdog water ??this is the ferulic acid. Any good vitamin C serum is likely to have a funky smell. I have a strong sense of smell, and I find the smell dissipates after no more than an hour following application. If you can stand it, it?ôs worth it!

column10: People who give this a bad rating obviously don?ôt know how to use it. It is not a 1 step and done cleanser. Think of this as a makeup remover. Rub it around and massage all over your face, focusing on eye makeup/stubborn areas. Then add water to hands and continue to massage. DO NOT RINSE. Now that the makeup and soap and oil are all mixed, you can go in with a wet wash cloth to wipe it away. Rinse your cloth and repeat, the makeup soap mixture will easily come off on the cloth and you can repeat these last rinsing steps until your face feels soap free. Set cloth aside and rinse face with one last splash of warm water. Then pat dry with clean towel. This is a type of DOUBLE CLEANSE and this is really the way people are supposed to used oil based cleansers. It?ôs the first step to breaking down makeup. When you?ôre done your face won?ôt be stripped because you started with the oil which protects your skin from the actual cleanser. The emulsification process is what removes the makeup when you massage the oil and cleanser together. Check youtube for videos of double cleansing. The last step after drying(for me) is to use a cotton pad with an essence/micellar water. When I do this I never see any makeup on the cotton pad except if I wore a lot of black eyeliner that day. Then it gets the remnants from the tiny crevices of my eyes. Hope this helps. Also I don?ôt like the bamboo scrub powder that comes with this because it contains corn starch. column10: I?ôve been using Luna, Good Genes, and UFO from Sunday Riley in my skin routine with only samples I?ôve been requesting every time I stop at a Sephora store, and these products really do work for me and my cystic acne, huge dark pores type skin. I do hate seeing reviews from people that tend to knock a product down without really understanding which products are even suitable for their own skin types. I rely on reviews myself and I try to leave ones only if I truly think it?ôs worth leaving. Anyways, it?ôs all about research research research! I?ôve always had acne prone skin and have been trying over the years to find products that work for me. Recently, I started to feel more hopeless than before because I?ôve been experiencing hormonal cystic acne for the first time along the sides of my face and thought what am I doing wrong? Instead of blaming my genetics or my diet or my stress levels I literally Googled, why am I breaking out along my jawline? Then, I found out about cystic acne, learned about AHA?ôs and BHA?ôs and how they actually work scientifically for the skin, and understanding those processes and what was happening to my skin internally helped me find products that I understood how to use and incorporate into my routine. And, it?ôs not a one product cures all type of deal. You have to address ALL the issues you have with your skin and understand which products to use in the morning, during the day, and at night. I literally have a bathroom counter with a ton of products for different uses. It sucks, but when you have clogged pores, acne scars, oily skin, and new acne type skin like me, you have to deal with it. At night, I deep clean, which is the best time to do so, using FRESH seaberry bar to initially cleanse, and then Boscia?ôs detoxifying black cleanser (which has glycolic acid in it...look that up!) with my Clarisonic brush. Afterwards, I apply Seabuckthorn oil from Poppy Austin thinly, let it soak in then I apply Luna by Sunday Riley gently tapping all over my face and jaw. After a couple minutes of Luna soaking in, then I apply Good Genes to seal the deal. I try to sleep head up to avoid my pillows absorbing anything out. Waking up my skin is amazing. In the morning, I don?ôt do any deep cleaning because your skin just needs replenishing. I use FRESH soy milk cleanser (the thicker one not the clear gel). This cleanser you put on dry to the face like lotion then rinse off which is nice for thirsty skin after a deep cleansing night. After that I use the FRESH seaberry bar as a second gentle cleanser, and then with my hands only the Boscia black detoxifying cleanser (that has glycolic acid). So, at night clarisonic deep cleaning, in the morning hands only. I finish my morning routine with Seabuckthorn oil as a moisturizer and then I apply UFO by Sunday Riley, which has salicylic acid, all over gently tapping my face which also calms my cystic acne down. My skin gets oily during the day naturally so I use Boscia?ôs charcoal oil blotting sheets to stay fresh until the night. So, to summarize sort of, Luna has Retinol which is good for acne, acne spots. UFO has salicylic acid, which is good for penetrating oil in pores and decongesting clogged pores. Good Genes has lactic acid which is good for exfoliating dead skin and more if I remember. And, Boscia has glycolic acid which is good for cell turnover like for acne scars. These are all mostly AHA?ôs and BHA?ôs so look them up. And seabuckthorn oil has omegas and great nutrients that help with rosacea, redness, acne; look that up too! It?ôs all about the right products, the right times of day, and moderation, don?ôt overdo the deep cleaning and remember to replenish skin with gentle cleansers and moisturizers. Ok I?ôm done.

It can only be cured with more sleep. However this product is very hydrating, my skin does look very smooth and bright and healthy. I do not experience any sensitivity nor congestion from this product. Would I continue use: Yes. Probably will be my number 1 anti aging eye cream for years to come. 100% recommend to everyone.

(Avobenzone protects similarly, but only for a short time, as it is an extremely unstable ingredient that breaks down quickly in sunlight.) So, if you feel this formula isn?ôt sophisticated enough for the pricetag, reconsider. This is an exceptionally sophisticated and beautiful formula considering how well it protects, and considering that zinc oxide is the most notoriously difficult sunscreen ingredient out there to formulate in terms of aesthetic appeal and wearability.
